name: Focusing question classifier
summary: A BERT classifier from Stanford that finds focusing questions in a teacher's turn, the questions that ask students to reflect on their own thinking, trained on raters' labels from math lessons.
grades: not stated (trained on 4th and 5th grade math lessons)

license.note: Stated in its card's metadata, which is all the card holds. The labelled data in its GitHub repository are MIT (funneling-focusing-questions).

access_note: About 440 MB, not gated. Edu-ConvoKit 0.4.0 calls it ddemszky/focusing-questions, which now leads here.
cite: Alic, S., Demszky, D., Mancenido, Z., Liu, J., Hill, H., & Jurafsky, D. (2022). Computationally Identifying Funneling and Focusing Questions in Classroom Discourse. BEA 2022, 224-233. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2022.bea-1.27

fits.how: Marks the turns where the AI asks a focusing question: the Edu-ConvoKit component runs it on the person's own computer once they download it. Its paper's best model, a RoBERTa, correlated .76 with experts; this released one is a BERT.

connect.note: Runs in the Edu-ConvoKit component's detector (edu-convokit) once you download it yourself. It is non-commercial, so it stays each person's choice and out of any package. Trained on classroom talk; nobody has checked it on chats with an AI.
